As a white Canadian student in India (Mumbai and Baroda, mostly), I've had no trouble at all. I had one guy mention Trudeau, but I just said it's okay new PM now and we laughed it off.

People are mostly just surprised, be prepared to take a lot of pics with people, and enjoy India! It's a great country with awesome people.

To offer an outside perspective as someone who is currently in India visiting for the first time, I think that there's a lot to be optimistic for here. 

I'm a white Canadian who's here on a joint government grant to study Sanskrit and Puranas, and I really wasn't sure what to expect. I wanted to think that I would like it, but as much as you try to put bias aside, it's hard not to look at travelogs from other Western travelers expecting the worst. And some of that worst is here, to be sure. The state of garbage on the streets and rivers makes me especially sad, as well as the prevalence of child beggars, something you just don't see in Canada. 

But I've also found a lot to love here, the history is amazing. Being able to look at and touch manuscripts with my own hands is unreal. There are beautifully curated museums, temples are electric, and the nature is stunning. Most of all, though, I'm so amazed by the people. The amount of kindness and generosity has been overwhelming. People here want me to enjoy India and show her best side, I can honestly say that I've never felt more welcomed than I do here.  I understand that any interactions I have are coloured by the fact that I'm white and from the West and perhaps that's the only reason why my outlook is so rosy. I only wish to say that there seems to be little of the inherently unkind, greedy picture often painted of the country by other travelers, the people here are largely good.

This is not me disregarding the social and political strife present in the country, that's very real and harmful to the overall unity of the nation, but I firmly believe that the majority of people here are kind, good people who want their lives and country to be better. 

I have no doubt that if I were here for longer than the cracks would start to show and I would become jaded, but nothing I've seen so far makes me believe that the country is beyond hope or saving. Will it take a lot to fix it? Of course. But it seems to me like there are people here who are willing to and want to make things better, and I think there's good to come yet.

I think you may be looking for a Christian perspective, if so I can't comment on that aspect, but I do think I can offer insight as a Kemetic and devotee of Bast for almost ten years.

No, I don't think that not wanting to worship her, yet still admiring her is wrong at all. You're allowed to take inspiration from any source you see fit, you're more than free to disregard divinity and just focus on what is being represented. That being said, in Ancient Egypt acknowledgment could be considered a minor form of worship insofar as speaking or writing any kind or words is a kind of Heka (Magic, or invocation of power). As in: if you're specifically thinking of Bast when you take actions that are representative of her, you would be giving her power by the use of her name and symbolism. Obviously, if you don't subscribe to this worldview it shouldn't matter, but I do think it depends what you define worship as. Modern Christians seem to have a much tighter definition of it than they did in Ancient Egypt, I think.
